precepts.text: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! A lot of times we as the prophets do not understand the magnitude of our calling, what we have been called to do. The Lord said he would send us as saviours, and our people's salvation will come no other way but by the prophets, by the saviours that God sent, and through his word. There is no way for the people to be saved unless the saviours are sent.
precepts.point: And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth. Our job is to raise up the tribes and restore the preserved of Israel. A light to the Gentiles: that is the scattered Israelites. That thou mayest be my salvation: that you may be a saviour.

note.label: Give Diligence

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord formed his servant from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him”, “to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”, “that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That you may be a saviour. A lot of times we, the prophets, don’t understand the magnitude of our calling. The Lord said he would send us as saviours, and our people’s salvation will come no other way than by the prophets, the saviours God sent, and through his word. Paul shows why.

“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?” This shows the importance of the prophets, the saviours: there is no way for the people to be saved unless the saviours are sent. “and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?”

We have been sent, throughout the four corners of the earth, and from the beginning, to be saviours. By going forth and teaching God’s word, salvation comes here on earth. “as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace.”

That is why the prophets of God are “glorious in the eyes of the Lord.” There is no higher calling than being a prophet of the Most High God, once he has revealed his son in you at the appointed time. Some of us used to be athletes, and once Christ was awakened in us we let all that go. None of it compares to what we do now in these last days as watchmen of Israel. This is the true glory, glorious not to man but to God, and our God is our strength to raise up the tribes of Jacob.

precepts.text: The Christian will say Romans 10:4 cancels out Deuteronomy: Christ is the end of the law for righteousness. No. Christ is the end of the law of animal sacrifice for righteousness; Christ took the place of the animal sacrifice. Verse one gives the context: my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved. We do not run from scriptures; we explain and edify on the scriptures.
precepts.point: And such were some of you: everybody in here can identify with something on that list and say, I used to do that. But ye are washed, but ye are sanctified, but ye are justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God. We are washed with the word of God.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
The Christian says, oh no, that's not the righteousness; go to Romans 10:4: “For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.” See, we ain't got to keep no laws, so that cancels out Deuteronomy 6:25. No, numbskull. We don't run from scriptures; we explain and edify on the scriptures.

Christ is the end of the law of animal sacrifice for righteousness. Christ took the place of the animal sacrifice. And where they think they have you, “to every one that believeth”, read verse one for the context: “Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.”

The whole subject is Israel being saved. Israel had “a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge”, “going about to establish their own righteousness”. Christ is our righteousness in the law because he suffered and took the place of the law of sacrifice. That does not do away with the commandments of Deuteronomy 6:25; it is why the unrighteous, who will not keep them, still shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

precepts.text: Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god: that white image is a strange god. He shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for gain: the land of Africa was divided for gain, exactly as written.
precepts.point: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? Our people have believed in a strange god, a eurocentric god. We are the only race that has a god that does not look like us.

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed?” How can our people call on the Almighty God that loves them when they have not believed in that God? Our people have believed in a strange god, a Eurocentric god. We are the only race that has a god that does not look like us. The God we serve is not the same God as the white man.

Daniel shows it: “Thus shall he do in the most strong holds with a strange god, whom he shall acknowledge and increase with glory”. That white Jesus is a strange god. “And he shall cause them to rule over many, and shall divide the land for gain.” The white man divided Africa for gain. That is what the Bible says he did.

Why is that god strange? Because he does not look like you. He has no laws, statutes or commandments. And he whooped you in slavery. We know that was the white man, yet we run on Sunday morning and pray faithfully to the same white man that shot us down in the streets and raped our mothers and fathers. Strange god.

“And how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?” Because we have been following a strange god all our lives, someone must be sent. That is why we send brothers out, only brothers with a good name: “How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” The glad tidings are that you are the Israelites, Christ died for you and your race, and he is coming back to save our race.

precepts.text: How shall they hear without a preacher, and how shall they preach except they be sent? Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth.
precepts.point: The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul; the testimony is sure, making wise the simple. People hunt for discrepancies over how many horses Solomon had, but the ten commandments are perfect and only the law converts the soul.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
David says “Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge”, and “Their line is gone out through all the earth”. You might think that speech and knowledge is the sun, the moon and the stars. No, it is the teachers, brothers out teaching day by day and night by night. Paul broke it down for us so we don't have to do guesswork: “But I say, Have they not heard? Yes verily, their sound went into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.” Paul is quoting Psalm 19, and their sound is the sound of teaching.

Start at verse 14: “How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?” Our people cannot call on the Lord if they have not heard. You need a preacher to hear this gospel. “And how shall they preach, except they be sent?” To preach is to prophesy, and it takes being sent. “How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!” That is why brothers are told: be prepared. Prepare yourself to be sent.

“Lord, who hath believed our report?” The report is the Bible, the scriptures. The prophets preach the report, and the question is who has believed it.

“So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” That is how you increase faith. New brothers and sisters ask how to increase their faith: you must consistently addict yourself to the hearing of the gospel, over and over. However old you are, calculate it: that is how many years of brainwashing you must undo. Coming in once a week will not undo it. It must be daily listening to the word, and reading more than the four chapters a day.

And whose sound is going into all the earth? All praises to the Lord for favouring this teaching. The doctrine of having sex with as many women as you can and not taking care of the babies is not going throughout all the earth. The groups talking about raping women and having concubines, the garbage teaching that John the Baptist is a wicked Israelite, the teaching that we are under the old covenant of animal sacrifice: none of that is going throughout the earth. The line that has gone out is repentance for the twelve tribes of Israel in the name of our king whom the world calls Jesus the Christ, heard now in all languages.

precepts.text: My heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is that they might be saved.
precepts.point: Sing with gladness for Jacob and say, O Lord, save thy people, the remnant of Israel. Salvation in the Bible is named over a people, and the churches have been deceiving people for centuries on it.

note.label: The Fallacy of Black Christians

precepts.text: Christ is the end of the law for righteousness; that goes into the sacrificial law.
precepts.point: Leviticus 7 answers it in context: whosoever eateth the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord shall be cut off. This is the law of sacrifice, which we are no longer under; Christ is the end of the law for righteousness. The sacrifices stopped after 70 AD at the fall of Jerusalem, when there was no longer a temple. And there is no way to take off all the fat of the meat you eat; we are not koshering our meat.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
“Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.” That goes into the sacrificial law, which the fat of Leviticus 3:17 belongs to.

The sacrifices stopped after 70 AD at the fall of Jerusalem, when there was no longer a temple. So the statute about the fat of the offering is not a statute we are cut off under today.

precepts.text: None can call on the Lord unless they believe, none believe unless they hear, and none hear without a preacher who is sent to guide and instruct.
precepts.point: No one comes to the truth alone; the Most High set up a structure of instruction, and a person must be taught the word rather than claiming private revelation.

note.label: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully

precepts.why:
“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?”

None can call on the Lord unless they believe, none believe unless they hear, and none hear without a preacher who is sent to guide and instruct. That is Jehoash: he “did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him.”

No one comes to the truth alone. The Most High set up a structure of instruction, and a person must be taught the word rather than claiming private revelation.

precepts.text: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
precepts.point: Hearing the word gives courage still, for we teach our people who they are, that the Israelites and the Christ are black. Faith comes by hearing.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 15: The Covenant to Seek the Most High

precepts.why:
“So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.”

“when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage”, put away the abominable idols out of Judah, Benjamin, and the cities he took from mount Ephraim, “and renewed the altar of the Lord.” Hearing the word gave him courage to act.

Hearing the word gives courage still, for we teach our people who they are, that the Israelites and the Christ are black. Faith comes by hearing.

precepts.text: Paul's heart's desire and prayer for Israel is that they might be saved, because he was writing to the Israelites in the Roman provinces.
precepts.point: This refutes the claim that the Old Testament is done away with, because everything the apostles preached was precept upon precept out of the law and the prophets.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Peter addresses the men of Israel, and Paul has the same people in mind when he writes to Rome: “Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.” He was writing to the Israelites in the Roman provinces, and his prayer was for Israel.

The audience never changed. These are the same people who asked in Acts 1:6 whether the kingdom would be restored to Israel. Peter proves who Christ is by walking through the prophecies of the Old Testament, and today we walk through those same prophecies to prove who Israel is.

That refutes the claim that the Old Testament is done away with. Everything the apostles preached was precept upon precept out of the law and the prophets.

precepts.text: Christians quote, confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in thine heart, but they miss that the whole argument was believing on Christ in replacement of animal sacrifice.
precepts.point: As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them; only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They first had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice, believing that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, which is why the apostles keep saying to repent and believe in his name.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
Christians quote it: “if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.” But they miss what the whole argument was. Believing on Christ was believing on him in replacement of animal sacrifice, that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not.

The Samaritans being baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus is that same believing. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, not doing away with the laws.

precepts.text: Paul's heart's desire and prayer for Israel is that they might be saved, defining the "whosoever."
precepts.point: The "whosoever" is whosoever of Israel, of Zion, because Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel to be saved, and the stone laid in Zion is Christ, so those who believe on him shall not be ashamed.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Peter ends his rehearsal of Christ's ministry with this: “To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.” The whosoever is whosoever of Israel, of Zion.

Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel: “Brethren, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.” That defines the whosoever. The salvation he is speaking of is Israel's.

precepts.text: The scripture saith, whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.
precepts.point: The "whosoever" is whosoever of Israel, of Zion, because Paul opens the same subject praying for Israel to be saved, and the stone laid in Zion is Christ, so those who believe on him shall not be ashamed.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“For the scripture saith, Whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed.”

Paul says this in the same chapter where his prayer is for Israel to be saved. The scripture he is quoting is the stone laid in Zion, and the whosoever that believes on that stone is whosoever of Zion, whosoever of Israel.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 19 Supper, War & Marriage

precepts.why: A lot of y’all stumble through Romans 10. Brothers, when you start teaching you’ll get hit upside the head with this verse. “For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth”: a brother in the class answers, the sacrificial law. When you sacrificed, your sins were to be forgiven; in Moses you got some sins forgiven but not all, and in Christ you got them all taken away. “That the man which doeth those things shall live by them”: if you could do those things under the old covenant you would live by them, but it was impossible for us to do it. “Say not in thine heart, Who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down from above:)”: because you don’t believe the Son of God came, taught us and sacrificed his life for us.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: Paul gave us the secret to increase our faith: “So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” If you spend all your time listening to Biggie Smalls or Drake, your faith is going to be very weak; if you spend your time listening to scriptures and classes, that will increase your faith, because you are feeding your spirit with the word of the Lord.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why: “First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people”: Paul is reminding us about the song of Moses, which you were supposed to tell your children’s children. “I was found of them that sought me not”: those were the Gentile Israelites in idolatry, worshipping wood and stone; the apostles went to them and said you’re the Israelites, repent, and they started to change their lives. “But to Israel he saith”: to the Israelites that knew the law and the commandments, “All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
One part says read, one part says hear. We did the reading already; let's talk about the hearing. Hearing is good; hearing builds faith. Many times you men and women ask, how do I build my faith? Paul gave you the secret. “So then faith cometh by hearing,” Faith comes by what? By hearing. Just like your children will know every Barney song, every Sesame Street song. When I was young they had Schoolhouse Rock: I'd be taking a test and I'll be like, conjunction junction, what's your function; I'm just a bill, sitting here on Capitol Hill. I learned by hearing. Me just reading, I couldn't retain it, but through music, through hearing, I retained it.

“and hearing by the word of God.” In case you're confused about what you should be hearing to build your faith, he says hearing by the word of God. You got to understand your own particular learning curve. Some of you can read and retain; some of us cannot, some of us must hear to retain. You got to know what works for you. I can't sit up late and read: you ever start reading and the devil jumps on you and you fall asleep? That's the damn devil. But if I'm listening I can stay awake, oh okay, I'm going to write that down, rewind that. Everybody ain't the same, so don't be comparing yourselves to each other; we all got a different learning curve.

You're going to find out with the kids: all kids don't learn the same. The women have to figure out what works for this particular child. That's why a lot of times black teachers are better than European teachers: they invest themselves in the children learning and try to figure out what allows this child to learn, as opposed to another one, rather than say, oh, they got ADHD, just give a medication. No, you got to figure out what makes this child tick, what makes him learn, what makes her learn.

points: So what? Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. Oh, faith cometh by hearing. And hearing, we're able to process what we heard, learn from it, and apply it to our life. So faith can increase by you hearing the word of God. Watch this. Deuteronomy 31:11.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

points: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God. So ask yourself, how often are you hearing the word of God? Do you watch videos? Do you read? Do you talk to brothers and sisters, actually going over scriptures? Because a lot of times we do speak to brothers and sisters but we talk about all kinds of nonsense that we watched on TV the night before.

Are we putting ourselves in a situation where the scripture becomes our life? The people we choose to converse with, are scriptures coming out? On our own free time, do we listen to the audio Bible, or read the Bible, or listen to classes? And as we are listening to classes, are we writing down the things we do not understand? Because a lot of times people read and study, but you realise they never have any questions. So that means you are the grand poobah of the scriptures. You understand everything the moment you open this Bible and read it? You are in a very bad place if your mind operates that way. I do not understand everything I read. So why do some of you read, read, read, but never have any questions?

You want to increase your faith, stop being full of yourself. Things you do not understand, write them down. You should have a page you just call questions. Every time you notice something you do not understand, write it down. That way when the time comes, you are in a position where you can ask questions. We are not going to answer all the questions in one day, but at least you always have something. That is how you grow.
